_source: Re-extracted from the real game after a playtest proved the previous file wrong. The 'GameData' Story/Level XML is stored as plain readable text inside SH_Data/resources.assets (no decompiler needed for this part -- found via `strings`/grep on the raw .assets file, then parsed as XML). That extraction has 49 <Level> elements total, not 34: LevelSetup.LoadStoryLevels() assigns LevelInfo.ID as a straight, unfiltered index over ALL of them (confirmed by decompiling LevelSetup.cs), including 'SHMenu' and many '_SEGWAYSTUB' dialogue-interlude entries this file deliberately excludes. 'gameId' below is that real index for each entry -- the mod's actual runtime join key (see mod/SuperhotArchipelago/Core/LevelCatalog.cs's LevelEntry.LevelId) -- and is NOT 'order - 1'; a real playtest proved that formula wrong (completing 'Kick', order 1, was reported as 'Dark Alley' complete, order 2; unlocking 'Cage Fight', order 8, visually lit up 'Jump', order 6). 'name' now carries the real native numbering, extracted from each Level's 'name' attribute (a loc key like 'GameData.Story.Level.name.01KICK_LVL' -- the embedded number/code IS the actual in-game display text for most entries, cross-checked against real hub screenshots). 'hasSecret' is extracted from the same XML's 'secrets' attribute per <Level> (confirmed via decompiling LevelSetup.cs: element.Attribute("secrets") -> LevelInfo.Secrets) -- every level in the real data has either 0 or 1, never more, so this is a plain bool rather than a count.
_caveats: Four scene names still appear more than once (TheyAreYourTools_C_2 x3, 'LevelTest#77 HackerRoom' x2) -- harmless now since matching is by gameId, not scene name.

'Dog1'/'Dog2'/'Dog3' all use numbers confirmed by real in-game observation (99/98/99 respectively), which do NOT match their raw loc-key numbers (08DOG1_LVL, 12DOG2_LVL, 18DOG3_LVL) -- the localized display evidently overrides the key's embedded number for these three secret/bonus entries. Dog1 and Dog3 both being '99' is confirmed correct, not a typo -- same pattern as the native '32' reuse below.

Both 'Cyberspace' entries (raw gameId 29 and 45) were REMOVED entirely, confirmed dead by real playtest: order-33 'Cyberspace (2)' gave 'a nothing check' with no real level behind it, and both were already flagged intermission="true" in the source XML (same as the '_SEGWAYSTUB' entries this file excludes) -- piOsMenu.AppendLevelData() explicitly skips IsIntermission levels, so they could never get a hub button regardless of unlock state. User confirmed only 32 real playable levels exist, which matches exactly once these two are dropped. Every 'order' value below was renumbered 1-32 to close the gap -- this changes every subsequent level's Archipelago location/item id (BASE_ID + order in Items.py/Locations.py), so any seed generated from an older levels.json is no longer id-compatible with this one; not a concern yet since no real seed has shipped, but worth remembering if that changes.

Order 34 (the real ending, now order 32)'s raw loc key has no number at all (just 'HACKERG_LVL'), but the actual displayed/save name is '34FREE.lvl' -- confirmed independently from real save file contents inspected earlier in this project (highestfinishedLevel: "34FREE.lvl"), same kind of localized-display-overrides-raw-key pattern already seen for Dog1/Dog2/Dog3. Named '34 - Free' here to match (kept as-is despite the renumbering above, since it's a display name copied from the game's own save data, not derived from our 'order' field).
'hallOfFame' (native code 14SERV) is possibly a non-combat/bonus scene rather than a real playable level -- unconfirmed.

The native numbering genuinely reuses '32' for two different levels ('Longway' and 'Core') -- confirmed in the source data itself, not an extraction error. 'Core' is the real in-game name confirmed by playtest, replacing this file's earlier guess of 'Passage' (title-cased from the raw loc-key code '32PASSAGE', which turned out not to be what's actually displayed).

LevelSetup.GetNextLevelInfo() does zero intermission-skipping outside of GameplayModifiers challenge mode -- it's just the literal next raw entry after CurrentLevelInfo, which for several of these levels (e.g. '05 - Subway' -> raw gameId 6, '28 - Station' -> raw gameId 35) is an untracked interstitial, not the next tracked level. The mod's LevelAccessGuard.ResolveToTrackedLevel() now walks forward past those before checking unlock state -- see mod/SuperhotArchipelago/Core/LevelAccessGuard.cs. This file doesn't need to represent those gaps (gameId isn't required to be contiguous), just noting why gaps in the gameId column are expected and intentional, not bugs.

hasSecret is false for exactly the 5 levels that also happen to share a duplicate scene name with another tracked level (Dog1/Dog2/Dog3 all 'TheyAreYourTools_C_2', Hacker and Free both 'LevelTest#77 HackerRoom') -- confirmed this isn't a coincidence worth worrying about: the native secret-found save key is 'SceneFileName + SecretNumber + "unlocked"' (see TerminalActivator.OnActivate), which WOULD collide across those duplicates if any of them actually had a secret. None do, so this never triggers in practice. The mod's own secret-check reporting still joins on LevelInfo.ID rather than scene name regardless, same as everything else in this file, so it wouldn't be affected even if that changed later.
